venue.name: CFB Esquimalt Naval and Military Museum
venue.description: The CFB Esquimalt Naval & Military Museum is located at Naden on Canadian Forces Base Esquimalt and collects, preserves, interprets and displays the history of the naval presence on Canada's West Coast and of the military on southern Vancouver Island. Its exhibits focus on Canada's Navy on the West Coast, the Canadian Women's Army Corps, the Women's Royal Canadian Naval Service and the West Coast Defences, and it houses an archive and library of photographs, ship plans and documents. The Oriole Children's Gallery is a hands-on room designed for children aged 4 to 8. Admission is by suggested cash donation and the museum sits inside a working military base, so visitors may need to show government photo ID to get in.

programs.name: Guided group tour
programs.description: The museum coordinates guided and self-guided tours of its exhibits and displays and takes tour requests from visiting groups; staff will work with the group to tailor a tour. There is a $75 standard fee for guided tours and a discounted fee of $50 for seniors' tours. The museum states it can negotiate reduced fees for tours, or waive fees entirely, for groups and organizations with limited funds. Tours are also provided to Fleet School students and other personnel taking courses at CFB Esquimalt.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the exhibit rooms with a guide, looking at ship models, uniforms, a submarine control display and cases of naval instruments such as a sextant and an optical range finder.
programs.our_note: The $75 is a flat fee for the tour rather than a charge per child, so it lands very differently on a group of eight than on a class of thirty. The museum says outright that it will negotiate or waive the fee for groups with limited funds, which is worth raising in your first email. Getting onto the base takes time. Allow about ten minutes on foot from the Naden main gate, and expect adults to be asked for photo ID.
programs.practical_summary: A flat tour fee, indoors, on a military base that requires photo ID at the gate. Nothing is published about washrooms, a lunch room, stroller or wheelchair access, or bus parking, so all of that needs a phone call.
programs.extra_fees_note: A discounted fee of $50 applies to tours for seniors. The museum can negotiate reduced fees for tours, or waive fees entirely, for groups and organizations with limited funds.
programs.evidence: There is a $75 standard fee for guided tours, and a discounted fee of $50 for tours for seniors.

programs.name: School visit and guided tour
programs.description: The museum will work with a class's curriculum to provide students with a learning experience, and directs teachers to its listing on the BC Field Trips site. Guided tours for school groups are offered free of charge in November as part of the museum's Remembrance Day programming; no fee is published for school tours in other months. Two downloadable quizzes are offered as teacher resources: a tri-fold quiz with text and images for elementary and middle school classes, and a more advanced general knowledge quiz for older students, both in English only.
programs.what_children_do: Move through the galleries with a guide and work through the museum's printed quiz, matching images and text to the displays.
programs.our_note: November is the month this becomes free, and it is also the month every other school in the region is thinking about Remembrance Day, so book early. Print the kids' quiz before you go. It is the only structured activity the museum publishes, and it turns a case-by-case walk into something a class can do. Nothing about group size, tour length or a booking deadline is published, so the first email should ask all three.
programs.practical_summary: Free guided tours in November only; the rest of the year the standard tour fee is the published figure. No lunch space, washroom, accessibility or capacity information is published at all.
programs.extra_fees_note: Free of charge applies to guided school tours in November only. No price is published for school tours in other months; the $75 standard guided tour fee is the only other published figure.
programs.evidence: Guided tours for school groups are offered free of charge in November, as part of our Remembrance Day programming.

programs.name: Oriole Children's Gallery (self-guided)
programs.description: The museum's Oriole Gallery was designed specifically with children in mind and offers imaginative activities for youngsters between 4 and 8 years. Published gallery features are dress-up play 'uniforms', an introduction to naval terms, diver gear (flippers, masks) and life jackets, games and a magnet board, signal flags and activities, and nautical-themed books for children. Admission to the museum is by suggested cash donation: Adults $10, Seniors/Students $5, Families $25.
programs.what_children_do: Put on the dress-up 'uniforms', try on flippers, masks and life jackets, play the games and the magnet board, handle the signal flags, and sit with the nautical picture books.
programs.our_note: This one room is the reason to bring under-sixes; the rest of the museum is cases, text panels and models at adult height. Admission is a suggested donation rather than a set price, so ask what a group of that size is expected to give when you call. Remember too that the gate ID check applies to the adults, not the children.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors, hands-on, and pitched at exactly the daycare age band. No washroom, lunch space, stroller or capacity information is published, and the donation is suggested rather than fixed.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission is by suggested cash donation: Adults $10, Seniors/Students $5, Families $25. No group or per-child rate is published.
programs.evidence: The gallery offers imaginative activities for youngsters between 4-8 years.

images.caption: This turn of the century deep-sea diving helmet was a critical tool in the maintenance of military equipment installed across the unruly underwater terrain of the the Pacific Ocean.

gaps: price: no per-child or per-group school rate is published outside November, and museum admission is a suggested donation rather than a set fee, so the cost of bringing a group is not knowable from the site.
youngest age: the Oriole Gallery is described for ages 4 to 8 but the museum publishes no minimum age for a visit or a tour.
capacity: no maximum or minimum group size is published for any tour.
lead time: no minimum notice period is published for booking a group tour.
duration: no tour length is published.
lunch space: unknown — the site says nothing about where a group could eat.
washrooms: unknown — not mentioned anywhere on the site.
rain backup: not applicable in the usual sense (the museum is indoors) but not addressed on the site.
stroller and wheelchair access: not addressed anywhere on the site, which matters here because the museum occupies historic buildings on a base.
bus parking: not addressed; the directions PDF covers transit and driving to the main gate but not where a school bus would park.
The Contact page carries a COVID-19 temporary closure notice that appears to be stale (page last modified 2024-03-28) — recorded in conflicts rather than treated as current.

The tours page image galleries are lightbox links with no alt attributes, so no interior or activity photo could be recorded with an honest alt; the og:image (filename 'fbsmp', 1030x541) appears to be a social-media card and its content could not be confirmed, so the hero was taken from the captioned artifact photograph on the homepage instead.

Program-level booking email tatiana.robinson@forces.gc.ca is published on the tours and contact pages; the site-wide footer gives Info@NavalAndMilitaryMuseum.org, which is recorded as the venue default.
